en: I have never eaten sushi.
why: を follows the noun, and the plain past {食|た}べた comes right before ことが.

before: {田中|たなか}さんは{前|まえ}に
en: I hear Tanaka-san has been to Hokkaido before.
why: Place + へ + plain past {行|い}った + ことが + ある.

en: May I smoke in this room?
why: The pattern is te-form + も + いい.

before: {明日|あした}は{休|やす}みだから、
en: Tomorrow is a day off, so you don't have to get up early.
why: {早|はや}く describes {起|お}きる, and なくても is followed by いいです.

before: {病院|びょういん}へ{行|い}く{前|まえ}に、{予約|よやく}
en: You have to make a reservation before going to the hospital.
why: {予約|よやく}をし + なければ + なりません is a fixed pattern.

en: I can only read a little kanji.
why: しか comes after {少|すこ}し and needs a negative verb after it.

en: My older brother can speak English and French.
why: AとB + が + potential verb; と joins the first noun to the second.

before: {週末|しゅうまつ}、{友達|ともだち}と{映画|えいが}
en: I'm thinking of going to see a movie with friends this weekend.
why: {見|み}に comes before {行|い}く, and the volitional {行|い}こう takes と{思|おも}う.

before: {来年|らいねん}、{日本|にほん}の{大学|だいがく}
en: Next year I plan to study at a Japanese university.
why: Place + で, then the dictionary form する before つもりです.

before: {今年|ことし}の{夏|なつ}は{忙|いそが}しいので、
en: I'm busy this summer, so I don't plan to go anywhere.
why: どこにも needs a negative verb, and {行|い}かない comes before つもりです.

en: I think it will rain tomorrow.
why: The plain-form clause {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}る comes before と{思|おも}います.

en: If you take this medicine, your fever will go down.
why: {薬|くすり}を needs the verb {飲|の}めば, then the result {熱|ねつ}が{下|さ}がるでしょう.

en: Please call me when you get to the station.
why: {着|つ}い + たら makes the condition, then {電話|でんわ}をください.

before: この{道|みち}を{右|みぎ}へ
en: If you turn right on this road, there is a bank.
why: Dictionary form + と, then what you find: {銀行|ぎんこう}があります.

en: If you're going to Kyoto, the shinkansen is best.
why: {行|い}く + なら gives the topic, then the advice {新幹線|しんかんせん}がいいです.

before: {弟|おとうと}はいつも{音楽|おんがく}を
en: My younger brother always does his homework while listening to music.
why: ながら joins to the verb stem {聞|き}き, and して comes before います.

before: このアパートは{駅|えき}から{近|ちか}い
en: This apartment is close to the station and the rooms are big, so I like it.
why: し lists the first reason after {近|ちか}い; {部屋|へや}も{広|ひろ}い is the second reason before ので.

before: {母|はは}が{作|つく}ったケーキは
en: The cake my mother made looks very tasty.
why: For "looks ~", drop the い of おいしい and add そうです.

before: {天気予報|てんきよほう}によると、{明日|あした}は
en: According to the weather forecast, it will snow tomorrow.
why: Hearsay そうです follows the plain form {降|ふ}る.

en: It seems to be raining outside.
why: {雨|あめ}が comes before {降|ふ}っている, and the plain form comes before ようです.

en: It seems Yamada-san has caught a cold.
why: {風邪|かぜ}をひく is a set phrase, and the plain past comes before みたいです.

before: {来週|らいしゅう}のテストは
en: I hear next week's test is very difficult.
why: とても comes before the adjective, and らしい follows the plain form {難|むずか}しい.

en: I had a dog when I was a child.
why: {犬|いぬ} + を + plain past {飼|か}った + ことがあります.

en: Have you ever climbed Mt. Fuji?
why: {山|やま}に{登|のぼ}る, then ことがありますか.

before: {私|わたし}は{今|いま}まで{一度|いちど}も{病気|びょうき}
en: I have never missed school because of illness.
why: {病気|びょうき} + で gives the reason, then {学校|がっこう}を{休|やす}んだことがありません.

before: テストのとき、{辞書|じしょ}を
en: May I use a dictionary during the test?
why: {辞書|じしょ}を needs the verb {使|つか}って, then もいいですか.

en: If you get tired, you can rest a little.
why: {少|すこ}し comes before the verb, then te-form + も + いい.

before: {図書館|としょかん}の{中|なか}で
en: You must not eat in the library.
why: Te-form + は + いけません means "must not".

before: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}らなければ、{傘|かさ}を
en: If it doesn't rain, you don't need to take an umbrella.
why: {持|も}っていく is one verb, and なくても is followed by いいです.

before: {日本|にほん}では{家|いえ}に{入|はい}る{前|まえ}に、{靴|くつ}を
en: In Japan you have to take off your shoes before entering a house.
why: {脱|ぬ}が + なければ + なりません is a fixed pattern.

before: {今日|きょう}は{母|はは}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}なので、{早|はや}く
en: It's my mother's birthday today, so I have to go home early.
why: {家|いえ}に comes before {帰|かえ}る, and {帰|かえ}ら + なくては + いけません.

en: Having to take medicine every day is hard.
why: なければならない is one pattern, and の turns the clause into the subject before は.

en: I can put on a kimono by myself.
why: Dictionary form + ことができます means "can".

before: {弟|おとうと}はまだ{三歳|さんさい}なので、{一人|ひとり}で
en: My little brother is only three, so he can't dress himself.
why: A potential verb takes が, and {着|き}られ + ません is the negative.

before: ここから{富士山|ふじさん}
en: You can see Mt. Fuji well from here.
why: が must follow {富士山|ふじさん}, and よく comes before the verb {見|み}えます.

before: {田中|たなか}さんは{料理|りょうり}が{上手|じょうず}で、{何|なん}
en: I hear Tanaka-san is a good cook and can make anything.
why: {何|なん}でも is a set word, and hearsay そう follows the plain potential {作|つく}れる.

en: I can't swim, so I don't go to the sea.
why: {泳|およ}ぐことができない is the reason before ので, then {海|うみ}には{行|い}きません.

en: I have become able to read kanji.
why: Potential form + ように + なりました means "became able to".

before: {明日|あした}から{毎朝|まいあさ}
en: I'm going to start jogging every morning from tomorrow.
why: ジョギングをする, in volitional form しよう, then と{思|おも}います.

en: Just as I was about to go to sleep, the phone rang.
why: Volitional + とした means "was about to", then とき, then what happened.

before: {夏休|なつやす}みに{国|くに}へ
en: I'm thinking of going back to my country in the summer vacation.
why: Volitional {帰|かえ}ろう + と + {思|おも}っています.

en: Shall we go and eat lunch together?
why: Object を, then {食|た}べに before {行|い}く, and volitional {行|い}こう + か.

en: I think Tanaka-san won't come today.
why: The plain-form clause {今日|きょう}{来|こ}ない comes before と{思|おも}います.

before: この{本|ほん}は{子|こ}どもには
en: I think this book is a little difficult for children.
why: {少|すこ}し comes before the adjective, and the plain-form clause comes before と{思|おも}う.

before: {山田|やまだ}さんは{来月|らいげつ}
en: Yamada-san said she is getting married next month.
why: The plain-form quote comes before と{言|い}っていました.

after: 、{遅|おそ}くまでゲームをしてしまいました。
en: I meant to go to bed early tonight, but I ended up playing games until late.
why: Dictionary form + つもり + だった, then のに for "but".

en: I'm saving money because I plan to buy a car next year.
why: {車|くるま}を{買|か}うつもりで is the plan, and お{金|かね}を goes before ためています.

before: {私|わたし}は{大学|だいがく}を{出|で}たら、
en: I plan to work in Japan after I graduate from university.
why: Place + で, then dictionary form {働|はたら}く before つもりです.

en: If it were a little cheaper, I would buy this bag.
why: もう{少|すこ}し goes with {安|やす}ければ, and この comes before the noun かばん.

en: If I have time, I'd like to go with you.
why: {時間|じかん}が needs あれば, and the stem {行|い}き comes before たい.

before: {分|わ}からない{言葉|ことば}は、{辞書|じしょ}
en: If you look up words you don't know in a dictionary, you'll understand the meaning.
why: {辞書|じしょ}を needs a verb {調|しら}べれば, then the result {意味|いみ}が{分|わ}かります.

en: When work is over, let's go for a drink.
why: {終|お}わっ + たら is the condition, and {飲|の}みに comes before {行|い}きましょう.

en: When I grow up, I want to be a doctor.
why: {大人|おとな}になったら is the time, then {医者|いしゃ}になり + たい.

en: When you press this button, tea comes out.
why: Dictionary form + と, then the result お{茶|ちゃ}が{出|で}ます.

en: When spring comes, the cherry blossoms bloom.
why: {春|はる}になる + と, then the natural result {桜|さくら}が{咲|さ}きます.

en: If you're buying a computer, the shop in front of the station is good.
why: なら follows {買|か}う, and {駅前|えきまえ}の must come before the noun {店|みせ}.

en: If it's Sunday, I have time, so I can help.
why: なら follows the noun {日曜日|にちようび}, and {時間|じかん}がある is the reason before ので.

en: You must not look at your phone while walking.
why: ながら joins to the stem {歩|ある}き, and {見|み}ては comes before いけません.

before: {父|ちち}はいつも{新聞|しんぶん}を
en: My father always eats breakfast while reading the newspaper.
why: {新聞|しんぶん}を needs the stem {読|よ}み + ながら, and {食|た}べ comes before ます.

en: I work a part-time job while going to university.
why: {大学|だいがく}に{通|かよ}う, its stem {通|かよ}い + ながら, then アルバイトをしています.

before: {今日|きょう}は{雨|あめ}も{降|ふ}っている
en: It's raining and I don't have time, so I won't go out today.
why: し follows the first reason, then {時間|じかん}もない + から.

before: あのレストランは{高|たか}い
en: That restaurant is expensive and the staff aren't kind, so I won't go again.
why: し follows {高|たか}い, and the second reason ends with から.

before: {山田|やまだ}さんは{頭|あたま}も
en: Yamada-san is smart and good at sports; she is amazing.
why: {頭|あたま}もいい + し, then the second item スポーツもできる + し.

en: The sky is dark; it looks like it's going to rain.
why: Verb stem {降|ふ}り + そう + な comes before the noun {天気|てんき}.

en: Tanaka-san looked well.
why: {元気|げんき} + そう + な comes before the noun {顔|かお}.

en: The children are playing happily.
why: {楽|たの}しい drops い to make {楽|たの}しそうに, which describes the verb {遊|あそ}んでいます.

before: この{机|つくえ}は{古|ふる}くて、
en: This desk is old and looks like it could break at any moment.
why: {今|いま}にも goes with そう, and そう follows the stem {壊|こわ}れ.

en: According to the news, the trains have stopped.
why: ニュースによると is a set phrase, and the plain form {止|と}まっている comes before そうです.

before: {先生|せんせい}の{話|はなし}では、{来週|らいしゅう}
en: According to the teacher, there's a test next week.
why: テストが comes before ある, and hearsay そうです follows the plain form.

before: {田中|たなか}さんの{話|はなし}では、{駅前|えきまえ}の
en: According to Tanaka-san, the ramen at the shop in front of the station is very good.
why: {駅前|えきまえ}の must be followed by a noun {店|みせ}, and とても comes right before おいしい.

before: {誰|だれ}も{電話|でんわ}に{出|で}ません。{家|いえ}
en: Nobody answers the phone. It seems nobody is home.
why: {家|いえ} + に, {誰|だれ}も needs the negative いない, then ようです.

before: {部屋|へや}の{電気|でんき}が{消|き}えていますね。{山田|やまだ}さんは
en: The room light is off. It seems Yamada-san has already gone to bed.
why: もう comes before the verb, and the plain past {寝|ね}た comes before ようです.

en: Please try writing it the way the teacher said.
why: {言|い}ったように means "as (someone) said", then {書|か}いてみてください.

en: That person is as good at Japanese as a Japanese person.
why: Noun + みたいに describes how, then {日本語|にほんご}が{上手|じょうず}です.

before: {道|みち}が{込|こ}んでいますね。
en: The road is crowded. It looks like there was an accident.
why: {事故|じこ}があった is the plain-form clause before みたいです.

en: Today is a hot day, like summer.
why: {夏|なつ}みたいに describes {暑|あつ}い, which comes before the noun {日|ひ}.

before: {山田|やまだ}さんは{来月|らいげつ}
en: I hear Yamada-san is quitting the company next month.
why: {会社|かいしゃ}をやめる is the plain-form clause before らしいです.

en: Today is really spring-like weather.
why: Noun + らしい makes "typical of spring", and it comes before the noun {天気|てんき}.

en: The person I met at the station yesterday is my teacher.
why: The plain past {会|あ}った comes before {人|ひと}, and {私|わたし}の comes before {先生|せんせい}.

en: These are clothes my mother wore when she was young.
why: {若|わか}い comes before ころ, and the clause {着|き}ていた comes before the noun {服|ふく}.
